newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finns more positive to EU membership -paper.
newsitem.headline: Finns more positive to EU membership -paper.

text.p: Finns' attitudes towards membership of the European Union have turned more positive, daily Helsingin Sanomat reported on Thursday.
"Finns are moderately satisfied with membership of the European Union ... Finns' attitudes have turned more positive during the first two years of membership," the paper said.
It referred to an opinion poll carried out by Talostutkimus Oy in August among 977 people.
The fall in food and other prices as a result of Finland having joined the EU at the start of 1995 was regarded favourably by 71 percent of respondents. @
More than half of those polled, 58 percent, said EU membership had had a positive effect on Finnish exports to countries in the western world.
On the minus side, 61 percent said membership had affected Finnish agriculture negatively, Helsingin Sanomat said.
Asked about the impact of EU membership on employment, 71 percent were undecided while 17 percent said joining the union had had a positive effect and 12 percent thought the contrary.
